html:
The abbey founded by Benedict of Nursia on a hill above Cassino, between Rome and Naples, around 529, and the Rule he wrote for its monks.

Benedict's Rule set out a balanced life: fixed hours of prayer through day and night, manual work, reading, and obedience to an abbot, with moderation in food and sleep. It is often summed up as "pray and work". Pope Gregory the Great wrote Benedict's life, which spread his fame.

Over the next centuries the Rule became the standard for monasteries across the Latin West, pushed by Charlemagne's court. Benedictine houses copied classical and Christian books, ran schools and farms, and kept learning alive in the early Middle Ages. In the same year, 529, Justinian closed the pagan schools of Athens, a coincidence later read as one age handing over to the next.

The abbey was sacked by the Lombards around 577 and rebuilt many times. Allied bombing destroyed it in 1944, during the Second World War, and it was rebuilt again.
sum: The abbey founded by Benedict of Nursia on a hill above Cassino, between Rome and Naples, around 529, and the Rule he wrote for its monks.
